Synopsis:
Russia's central bank held its key rate at 14% ahead of parliamentary elections, balancing persistent inflation pressures — driven by Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries and e-commerce infrastructure, rouble weakness, and budget deficit concerns — against a near-stagnant economy expected to grow just above zero in 2026. Oil prices above $100 (linked to the unresolved U.S.-Iran conflict) provide some budget relief but domestic fuel price mechanisms limit pass-through inflation. No pre-election fiscal stimulus is planned, unlike prior election cycles.
